recent_posts.title: Tumbleweed Monthly Update - April 2026
recent_posts.summary: openSUSE Tumbleweed's April 2026 monthly update covers a wide range of package updates and security fixes. Highlights include GNOME 50 and KDE Gear 26.04.0 as major desktop releases, GTK4 4.22 with a new native GtkSvg renderer dropping the librsvg dependency, Linux kernel advancing to 7.0.2, Mesa 26.0.4/26.0.5 with raytracing fixes, and LibreOffice 26.2. Developer-facing updates include PHP 8.5.5, SQLite 3.53.0, iproute2 7.0, and nano 9.0. Security received heavy attention with dozens of CVE fixes across WebKitGTK, CUPS, Python, Flatpak, sudo, OpenEXR, libxml2, libarchive, mozilla-nss, and more. The Copy Fail vulnerability affecting openSUSE flavors was also addressed.

recent_posts.title: openSUSE Asia Summit 2026 Call for Speakers
recent_posts.summary: The openSUSE Asia Summit 2026 Call for Speakers is now open. The event will be held on October 3–4, 2026, at Universitas Gadjah Mada in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Speakers from all backgrounds are invited to submit proposals on topics including openSUSE distributions, desktop environments, cloud/containers, security, IoT, and FOSS culture. Proposals must be 130–250 words in English, submitted by July 1, 2026, with speaker notifications on July 21. Travel support is available via the openSUSE Travel Support Program. In-person attendance is required; remote presentations are not accepted.

recent_posts.title: Quantum-Resilient Cryptography in the openSUSE Ecosystem
recent_posts.summary: libzupt, a new post-quantum cryptography SDK, has been officially released as a package in the openSUSE ecosystem (Leap and Tumbleweed). The library implements a hybrid ML-KEM-768 + X25519 approach for file and in-memory encryption, standardized by NIST in August 2024. It currently supports C++, Python, and Java (Node.js in development), aiming to make post-quantum cryptographic mechanisms accessible to developers. The library originates from the Zupt backup/compression project and is designed to help applications remain secure against future quantum computing threats such as Shor's Algorithm.

Other highlights include an update on ARMv9 build infrastructure in Open Build Service, OpenVINO 2026.1 release with expanded multimodal AI model support, KDE Plasma 6.6's new setup wizard, KDE Frameworks 6.25 release, GNOME app icon milestone of 120+ completed requests, a blog migration from Jekyll to Zola, syslog-ng streaming to data lakehouses via OpenTelemetry, and announcements for KDE Akademy 2026 in Graz.

recent_posts.title: Following Up on ARMv9 Build Infrastructure
recent_posts.summary: openSUSE's Open Build Service (OBS) has been running NVIDIA Grace Hopper hardware since last June, enabling native ARMv9 builds for Tumbleweed packages. The infrastructure now handles complex workloads including the Linux kernel, LLVM, GCC, Python, and Qt frameworks with good success rates. Native builds on actual silicon eliminate risks from emulated cross-compilation such as ABI mismatches and instruction scheduling errors. The post also makes a broader case for hardware vendors to donate or lend machines to OBS, framing it as a continuous automated QA benefit for vendors whose products run Linux.

recent_posts.title: Tumbleweed Monthly Update - March 2026
recent_posts.summary: openSUSE Tumbleweed's March 2026 monthly update covers a wide range of package updates and security fixes. Highlights include three KDE Plasma 6.6 point releases with progressive bugfixes to KWin, Spectacle, and Kicker; KDE Frameworks 6.24.0 with nanosecond-precision timestamps in KIO; Linux kernel progression from 6.19.5 to 6.19.9 with broad hardware and filesystem fixes; Mesa 26.0.2 resolving RDNA 4 visual corruption and a Counter-Strike 2 regression on Intel Arc; and GStreamer 1.28.1 adding speech-to-text transcription and AV1 decoding. Security was a major theme, with dozens of CVEs addressed across FreeRDP, curl, libsoup2, the kernel (ksmbd), Python, bind, ImageMagick, GraphicsMagick, exiv2, QEMU, and many more packages. libxml2 2.15.2 dropped its built-in HTTP client and aligned HTML serialization with HTML5.

recent_posts.title: openSUSE Leap 15 reaches end of life after nearly eight years
recent_posts.summary: openSUSE Leap 15.6 is reaching End of Life at the end of April 2026, closing out nearly eight years of the Leap 15 series that began with version 15.0 in May 2018. Users are advised to upgrade to Leap 16 to continue receiving security and maintenance updates. Leap 16 is expected to run through version 16.6 in Fall 2031, with 24 months of support per point release.

top_posts.title: Replace Windows, Not Your Device
top_posts.summary: With the end of Windows 10 support, users are encouraged to consider open-source alternatives like openSUSE instead of discarding functional hardware. Using Linux distributions can extend the life of devices, reduce electronic waste, and offer greater control over privacy and security without the need for new hardware.

top_posts.title: GSoC 2025, Building a Semantic Search Engine for Any Video
top_posts.summary: A GSoC 2025 project that built an end-to-end semantic video search engine capable of finding specific moments within videos using natural language queries. The system uses a two-part architecture: an ingestion pipeline that processes videos with AI models (TransNetV2, WhisperX, BLIP, VideoMAE) to extract shots, transcripts, captions, and actions, then segments them intelligently and enriches them with LLM-generated summaries; and a search application with FastAPI backend that performs hybrid text-visual searches using ChromaDB vector database and Reciprocal Rank Fusion for result ranking, paired with a Streamlit frontend for user interaction.

top_posts.title: Software Policies Can Fuel Waste
top_posts.summary: A viral Reddit photo showing pallets of discarded government PCs highlights how software policies create massive e-waste. These computers are being thrown out not because they're broken, but because they can't upgrade to newer Windows versions, despite being capable of running Linux distributions like openSUSE. The article advocates for the "Public Money, Public Code" principle, arguing that government adoption of open-source software could reduce taxpayer costs, extend hardware lifecycles, and prevent environmental damage from toxic e-waste. With Windows 10 extended support ending in October 2026, the "End of 10" campaign promotes transitioning to Linux as a fiscally and environmentally responsible alternative.

top_posts.title: gaming on openSUSE offers a great Linux experience
top_posts.summary: With Windows 10 nearing end-of-life, openSUSE offers a viable, cost-effective alternative for gaming on Linux. It supports popular Steam games via Proton and offers excellent hardware compatibility. Transitioning to openSUSE can extend the lifespan of your gaming rig while avoiding forced upgrades and contributing to e-waste.

top_posts.title: AI hands out Windows keys, but Linux never had a lock
top_posts.summary: AI's involvement in software piracy has highlighted the advantages of using free, open-source operating systems like Linux, particularly openSUSE. With the impending end of support for Windows 10, users can avoid licensing fees and extend hardware lifespans by switching to Linux, which offers a wide range of free applications and better compatibility with older devices. Businesses can also significantly reduce IT expenses by adopting open-source solutions.
